analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (lines 1–799) and the bounded patch. Existing assertions cover required-lane failures, recursive checkout, build execution despite cache hits, fixture prerequisites, native media and retention gates, coverage accounting, installer safeguards, and absence of backend credentials. These support artifact integrity and availability concerns in T-013, T-034, T-054 and TB-007; cache-related assertions do not themselves alter T-041's production encryption, authenticated scope, TTL or memory policy. No supplied change directly alters authorization, attestation, inference encryption, billing or consumer-data handling.
The visible addition at HEAD lines 155–187 introduces test constants/helpers for daily .git caching, connectivity validation, sparse checkout, and cache saving restricted to pushes on master/dev. This is test specification, not evidence that the workflow enforces those controls. BASE lines 714–717 and 788–795 show the older PR cache-save expectations, but their HEAD replacements and the actual workflow/action changes are not supplied here. No concrete security regression is independently established. Integration should examine .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml changes alongside the remaining HEAD test additions: verify cache provenance and branch isolation, restored Git metadata/config handling, checkout credential persistence, and preservation of fail-closed build/test gates. git fsck connectivity alone establishes neither trusted configuration nor cache provenance. The truncated patch and BASE-only primary units limit conclusions about the new implementation.
